note: The short walkthrough's voice copy: one sentence a row, read one wav a row so the voice pauses between sentences (Tys, 29 Oct: "the script doesnt seem to stop for pauses"); a scene's rows share its segment in the plan. This file is what the voice read; the Voice column in docs/demo/walkthrough.md is copied from it. 'say' is what the voice reads when it differs from the caption.

lines.text: Xenoform turns a song into a music video where every beat is a transformation.
Drop in a song and pick a vibe, or None, the things just as they are.
Then say what it morphs through.
A theme like underwater brings fifteen things of its own.
“Make” plans the shots on the song's bars and beats, and renders a morph for every shot.
lines.say: Make plans the shots on the song's bars and beats, and renders a morph for every shot.

lines.text: Every shot is one object turning into the next, cut to the song's own bars.
Five ways to change, and the change can land right on the beat.
Effects ride the kick and the loudness.
Then edit it like a timeline, shot by shot.
Colour, effects, order and cuts, re-cut from the cached morphs with no GPU.
Or morph film clips into each other: a free pack of public-domain films, or your own.
A Draft in minutes, a Fast Final at 1080p, or the full Final, here or on Comfy Cloud.
lines.say: A Draft in minutes, a Fast Final at ten eighty p, or the full Final, here or on Comfy Cloud.

lines.text: How it's built: the song is split into stems and bars.
The plan becomes ComfyUI graphs, sent through the Comfy SDK.
LTX renders every morph, on any card from 12 GB up, or on Comfy Cloud.
lines.say: LTX renders every morph, on any card from twelve gigabytes up, or on Comfy Cloud.

lines.text: All open weights, local by default.
What's new: the edit comes from the music itself.
Every shot is generated, and you change it like an editor, not a prompt box.
An MCP server lets any AI drive it.
Xenoform.
Open source, on GitHub.
